precepts.text: But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. And Saul's servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
precepts.point: So do not think just because you are here you may not be battling with that spirit right now. Just wait. You think the Lord wrote this in here for no reason? The Lord said if it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom. Now is that something where I am battling Sodom? No. The Lord said if it was not for the Lord we would all be as Sodom, all be in as destructive a state as Sodom and the cities of Gomorrah. We would all be worthy of that same destruction. So do not think, because you are not dealing with it right now, that spirit is going to tempt you at some point. The bitterness is going to tempt you. Hatred is going to tempt you. Unforgiveness is going to tempt you. Satan said, hold my cup.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Mark 7:22 names “an evil eye” among the evil things that come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” 1 Samuel 18:9 says “Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” Was it with the looks of righteousness, or with an evil eye? An evil eye. And that evil eye defiled Saul even further, after the Lord had already rejected him. To see it, go back to where Saul’s trouble began, in chapter 16.

“But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” Saul was already battling some things. The Lord had rejected him, and an evil spirit from the Lord had taken him.

“And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.” They told him: find someone who plays cunningly on a harp, and that spirit will leave you.

There are building blocks of bitterness. Bitterness doesn’t just come about; there are other things first. Saul rejected the word of the Lord, and the Spirit of the Lord departed from him. That was the ground the evil eye grew in. And don’t think, because you are not battling that spirit right now, that it won’t come. Satan says, hold my cup. Wait until you get the new job offer, the promotion, the demotion, the transfer to another school or another city, where you are dealing with different spirits and different circumstances, and you wonder why you are being troubled in the spirit. If it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom.

precepts.text: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him. So David did a good thing by playing the music to have that spirit depart from King Saul.

The Lord said if it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom. Now is that something where I am battling Sodom? No. The Lord said if it was not for the Lord we would all be as Sodom, all be in as destructive a state as Sodom and the cities of Gomorrah. We would all be worthy of that same destruction. So do not think, because you are not dealing with it right now, that spirit is going to tempt you at some point. The bitterness is going to tempt you. Hatred is going to tempt you. Unforgiveness is going to tempt you. Satan said, hold my cup.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.”

So David did a good thing by playing the music to have that spirit depart from King Saul. Saul did what the servants said, the spirit left him, and he was refreshed. He was like, man, I needed that. He was back in the spirit again. David was sent for Saul’s benefit, and Saul could not see it.

Now fast forward to chapter 18. Saul “eyed David from that day and forward”, and “it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul.” The very next day after he had an evil eye towards David, meaning he was ready to do harm to David, that evil spirit returned. “And David played with his hand, as at other times: and there was a javelin in Saul’s hand.” David had already done this for him, as at other times. “And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it.”

That is how quickly hatred can progress: the man whose playing made the evil spirit depart becomes the target of the javelin. That is Mark 7: “an evil eye” comes from within and defiles the man. The evil eye brought the evil spirit back, and the bitterness turned into an attempt to kill.

precepts.text: Then came together unto him the Pharisees and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem. Same thing done yesterday is being done this very day.
precepts.point: It says, then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees which were of Jerusalem: meaning they came from Jerusalem, following Christ around, from place to place. Cuz I said they follow from state to state; soon it'll be country to country. Don't be shocked.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account as Matthew 15:1: “Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.” They came from Jerusalem, following Christ around from place to place, gathering together against him.

The same thing done yesterday is being done this very day. Those who hate this truth follow these men the same way, from state to state, and soon it will be from country to country. Don't be shocked when you see it; the scribes and Pharisees did it to Christ first, travelling from Jerusalem to find fault with him.

precepts.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. Every one of them is dross and tin. All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together: wicked Israel gets the same judgment as Esau. They shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired: the idols. Confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen: the churches. As an oak whose leaf fadeth: your understanding is gone. As a garden that hath no water: no water of understanding. And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them: God gets rid of what he cannot use.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin.” Dross is waste, refuse, any worthless matter, and the tin goes with the dross. God will turn his hand upon us, the Israelites, and purge away everything within us that is wasteful and useless. What is that? Christ lists it.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”: from within, out of the mind of men. Evil thoughts: that is dross and tin. “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness”: every one of them is dross and tin. Add the rest we carry: lying, stealing, child molestation, masturbation, pornography, bestiality, anger, malice. All of it.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” The dross is not outside of us; it is in us, and that is what God is purging.

So that one verse speaks volumes. The “thee” God turns his hand upon is you and me, and what he purges away is everything that proceeds out of our own hearts and defiles us, so that afterward Israel can be called “The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

precepts.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts: that is how you know your heart is your mind, because evil thoughts do not come from the middle of your chest. Adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: all these evil things come from within, and defile the man. Definition read in class: lascivious describes someone or something driven by or tending to arouse unrestrained sexual desire; pornography falls under that.
precepts.point: In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands: when we accept Christ as our king and savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. Let Christ's words circumcise our minds.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Why must we circumcise the heart? What's in it? Christ says: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” That is how you know your heart is your mind. Your evil thoughts don't come from the middle of your chest; they come from your mind, your thoughts.

Then the list: “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.” Lasciviousness describes someone or something driven by, or tending to arouse, unrestrained sexual desire: indecent, lewd or lustful behavior, thoughts or expressions. Pornography is one of them; you could throw that word right in there. An evil eye is when you hate your neighbor.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That's what defiles us, all of us. So this is what is cut off in the circumcision made without hands: all these immoralities in the mind, put off “by the circumcision of Christ.”

precepts.text: The heart is the mind: the broken in heart are the broken in mind and spirit.
precepts.point: Missing a dollar-eighteen gas is wanting America to continue; the affliction has to happen, and when we see these things our salvation draws near.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
The psalm says the Lord “gathereth together the outcasts of Israel. He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” Who are the broken in heart? We are the ones broken in mind and spirit, because the heart is the mind. Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. Thoughts come out of the heart, so the heart is the mind.

The broken in heart are the broken in mind: the twelve tribes, the outcasts of Israel. And it is the Lord who “bindeth up their wounds”. Everything we went through in captivity, it is the Lord that will minister the ointment to fix and heal his nation. These other nations cannot fix you with their philosophies and doctrines; they don't care about us and do not want to restore us, because restoring us means giving back everything they spoiled from the children of Israel.

Many of our brothers and sisters feel the only way we will come together is by the hands of these other nations. But it is Christ who is coming to restore this glorious nation, build up Jerusalem, gather the outcasts, and heal the broken in mind.

precepts.text: Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost? Satan whispers thoughts and puts things in your head that are not there, even 'the deacon does not like you.' Every one of us gets attacked in the mind, the deacon included.
precepts.point: How do those evil things get into the mind? Acts shows it: Satan fills the heart.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Christ said evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders and the rest come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “defile the man.” So how do those evil things get into your mind? Remember who the war is against: Satan. Acts shows how he does it.

“But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost” What did Satan do? He filled his heart to lie. That lying spirit comes from Satan.

That is how he works. He is there in your head, whispering thoughts, tempting you, putting things there that are not there. The deacon says something to you and Satan says, why did he say that to you? The deacon don't like you. A husband gives his wife an order to clean the bathroom, and Satan whispers: you going to let him talk to you like that, after all you do in this house? He don't understand you; he don't love you. If she listens, she becomes bitter and it shows in her actions.

Satan puts things in everyone's head, the deacon included. The fight with Satan starts first and foremost in your mind, and many fall in this truth because they wait until the mind is already defiled. To win, you have to kill it right there: the thoughts Satan puts in your mind should never become action. Ask, why am I thinking like this? Fast and pray, Lord take these thoughts out of my mind, and answer him with the word of God, “the sword of the Spirit”, the weapon we fight with.

precepts.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Before the physical act comes the thought, and God counts the thought as breaking thou shalt not kill.
precepts.point: If your head is full of evil, maybe you are not reading enough. The brothers who do not know the scriptures are the ones who will betray you and plant things in your house. Young men, when did you and the brother you talk to all week last discuss scripture?

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
Christ lists what comes out of the heart of men, and murders is among them: “evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.” Some do not understand how murder can come out of the mind, so John makes it plain: “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

The hatred you carry is equivalent to murder. Where does it all begin? In your mind, as Mark 7 says. Before you ever commit the act of physical murder, it has to begin with a thought, and the thought of it is the exact same thing. The hatred we have as a people one for another: God says you're already a murderer. You already broke the commandment thou shalt not kill.

It works the same with adultery. The minute you see that ex at the grocery store and take his phone number, before you have even said anything, that is adultery right there. It starts in the mind.

Nobody knows you more than Messiah. He created you, so he knows what is in your mind. We cannot read your mind, but he can, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” So deal with the hatred while it is still a thought, because no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

precepts.text: Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness and the rest; they come from within and defile the man.
precepts.point: Every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust and enticed. Lust has nothing to do with love.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

precepts.text: From within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts; the heart is the mind.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The heart in scripture is the mind: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders”. Evil thoughts proceed from the heart, so the heart is the mind.

Sin is what makes a man dirty, nasty, and filthy, so the uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments. The uncircumcised heart of Leviticus 26 is the mind these things proceed from.

precepts.text: Out of the heart of man proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts and the rest; these come from within and defile the man, so a pure heart is not pondering these things.
precepts.point: Not lifting up the soul unto vanity nor swearing deceitfully means no lying, not telling a brother "I'ma pay you back" and never doing it.

note.label: Psalm 24: The King of Glory

precepts.why:
“He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart”. A pure heart is the mind, and Christ shows what comes out of the heart: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders”.

Evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts and the rest come from within and defile the man. So a pure heart is not pondering upon these things, because out of the heart the mouth speaks, and once the mouth speaks it you give life to it and will eventually do it.

Clean hands means he has not committed those sins, or has repented from them. A pure heart keeps them from ever being pondered in the first place.

precepts.text: Out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts, where evil begins.
precepts.point: Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.” Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, out of the heart.

So the strife the fool starts, the rebellion the evil man seeks, and the evil rewarded for good all flow from an evil heart. Leave off contention before it is meddled with, because what proceeds from that heart is confusion and every evil work.

precepts.text: The same account told in Matthew: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders?
precepts.point: There is no law in the scriptures that a man must wash his hands before he eats. That was a tradition of the elders, and the whole contention is about tradition, not about law.

note.label: Mark 7: The Tradition of the Elders and What Defiles a Man

precepts.why:
The Pharisees and scribes saw some of the disciples eat bread “with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.” They asked, “Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?”

Matthew tells the same account and puts the charge the same way: “Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” Notice the word in both: tradition. There is no law in the scriptures that a man must wash his hands before he eats. That was a tradition of the elders, and the whole contention is about tradition, not about law. The Pharisees themselves named it a transgression of the tradition of the elders, not of the law.

precepts.text: That same woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation.
precepts.point: Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
Mark tells what the woman of Canaan was: “The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.”

That same woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation, and to her Christ said he was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. So when Greeks come up to worship at the feast and are answered with prophecy, and when Grecians murmur against the Hebrews in the church, those are not Greeks by nation; they are Israelites of the Greek captivity.
